discovery: Programmable quantum matter with arrays of individually trapped Rydberg atoms

nominees.name: Antoine Browaeys
nominees.affiliation: Institut d'Optique Graduate School, CNRS, Université Paris-Saclay, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum simulation and quantum information
motivation: The nominees turned single neutral atoms, held in optical tweezers and coupled through the Rydberg blockade, into a platform for building and controlling quantum many-body systems atom by atom. Saffman made the first demonstrations of Rydberg blockade between two individual atoms and of neutral-atom entangling gates. Browaeys developed defect-free, reconfigurable two- and three-dimensional arrays and used them to simulate quantum magnetism with exceptional control. Lukin, who co-proposed the blockade mechanism, showed with these arrays new quantum phases, quantum many-body scars, topological spin liquids and logical qubits with error-correction circuits. Starting from basic atomic physics, the work has become a general tool for condensed-matter physics, quantum optics and quantum computing. It shows that AMO techniques can be used to engineer complex quantum states and to measure them one particle at a time.
